lesson_scope: Solving trigonometric equations involving reciprocal functions and quadratic substitutions using Pythagorean and double angle identities in degree and radian intervals.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving basic negative reciprocal secant equation in degrees.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Basic reciprocal conversion of secant to cosine.

hints: Cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III: $\theta = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$ and $\theta = 180^\circ + 60^\circ = 240^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Convert the reciprocal function to cosine:
$$\sec\theta = -2 \implies \cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$$

Find the reference angle in Quadrant I:
$$\alpha = \arccos\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 60^\circ$$

Identify solutions in Quadrants II and III for $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\text{Quadrant II: } \theta = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant III: } \theta = 180^\circ + 60^\circ = 240^\circ$$
$$\theta = 120^\circ, 240^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Converts $\sec\theta = -2$ to $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$ and identifies reference angle $60^\circ$.
Obtains $\theta = 120^\circ$ and $\theta = 240^\circ$ and no other solutions in the interval.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: solving multiple-angle cotangent equation in radians with exact values.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Reciprocal cotangent conversion with scaled angle domain.

hints: Find the interval for $2x$: since $0 \le x \le \pi$, we have $0 \le 2x \le 2\pi$.
Solve for $2x$: $2x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}$, then divide by 2 to get $x = \frac{\pi}{12}, \frac{7\pi}{12}$.

walkthrough.text:
Invert to tangent and state domain for $2x$:
$$\cot 2x = \sqrt{3} \implies \tan 2x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$
$$0 \le x \le \pi \implies 0 \le 2x \le 2\pi$$

Find all angles for $2x$ within $[0, 2\pi]$:
$$\text{Principal angle: } 2x = \arctan\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}$$
$$\text{Second angle: } 2x = \frac{\pi}{6} + \pi = \frac{7\pi}{6}$$

Divide by 2 to obtain $x$:
$$x = \frac{\pi}{12}, \quad x = \frac{7\pi}{12}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Converts $\cot 2x = \sqrt{3}$ to $\tan 2x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ and finds principal value $2x = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
Obtains exact solutions $x = \frac{\pi}{12}$ and $x = \frac{7\pi}{12}$ and no others in $0 \le x \le \pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: factorising and solving standard quadratic equation in cosine.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Factorising standard quadratic in cosine with special angle roots.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise the quadratic expression in $\cos\theta$:
$$2\cos^2\theta + \cos\theta - 1 = 0 \implies (2\cos\theta - 1)(\cos\theta + 1) = 0$$

Solve $\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}$ for $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\theta = 60^\circ, \quad \theta = 360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ$$

Solve $\cos\theta = -1$ for $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\theta = 180^\circ$$
$$\text{Combined solutions: } \theta = 60^\circ, 180^\circ, 300^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Factorises into $(2\cos\theta - 1)(\cos\theta + 1) = 0$ to get $\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}, -1$.
Obtains $\theta = 60^\circ$ and $\theta = 300^\circ$ from $\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}$.
Obtains $\theta = 180^\circ$ from $\cos\theta = -1$ and no other solutions.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: using Pythagorean identity tan^2(theta) = sec^2(theta) - 1 to solve quadratic equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Pythagorean substitution transforming mixed tan/sec into quadratic in sec.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the identity $\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta - 1$:
$$2(\sec^2\theta - 1) + \sec\theta = 1$$
$$2\sec^2\theta + \sec\theta - 3 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for $\sec\theta$:
$$(2\sec\theta + 3)(\sec\theta - 1) = 0 \implies \sec\theta = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad \sec\theta = -\frac{3}{2}$$

Solve each branch for $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\cos\theta = 1 \implies \theta = 0^\circ, 360^\circ$$
$$\cos\theta = -\frac{2}{3} \implies \text{ref angle } = \arccos(2/3) \approx 48.19^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant II: } 180^\circ - 48.19^\circ = 131.8^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant III: } 180^\circ + 48.19^\circ = 228.2^\circ$$
$$\theta = 0^\circ, 131.8^\circ, 228.2^\circ, 360^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies identity $\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta - 1$ to form quadratic $2\sec^2\theta + \sec\theta - 3 = 0$.
Solves quadratic to obtain $\sec\theta = 1$ and $\sec\theta = -\frac{3}{2}$ (or $\cos\theta = 1, -\frac{2}{3}$).
Obtains $\theta = 0^\circ, 131.8^\circ, 228.2^\circ, 360^\circ$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: using cosec^2(x) = 1 + cot^2(x) to solve quadratic equation in radians.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Pythagorean substitution transforming cosecant/cotangent into quadratic.

hints: Substitute $\operatorname{cosec}^2 x = 1 + \cot^2 x$ into $3\operatorname{cosec}^2 x - 5 = \cot x$.
Simplify to $3\cot^2 x - \cot x - 2 = 0$ and factorise: $(3\cot x + 2)(\cot x - 1) = 0$.
Solve $\cot x = 1 \implies x = \frac{\pi}{4}$ and $\cot x = -\frac{2}{3} \implies \tan x = -1.5 \implies x = \pi - \arctan(1.5) \approx 2.16$ rad.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $\operatorname{cosec}^2 x = 1 + \cot^2 x$:
$$3(1 + \cot^2 x) - 5 = \cot x$$
$$3\cot^2 x - \cot x - 2 = 0$$

Factorise the quadratic in $\cot x$:
$$(3\cot x + 2)(\cot x - 1) = 0 \implies \cot x = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad \cot x = -\frac{2}{3}$$

Solve in the interval $0 \le x \le \pi$:
$$\tan x = 1 \implies x = \frac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.785$$
$$\tan x = -1.5 \implies x = \pi - \arctan(1.5) = \pi - 0.9828 = 2.159 \approx 2.16$$
$$x = \frac{\pi}{4}, \ 2.16 \text{ rad}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies identity $\operatorname{cosec}^2 x = 1 + \cot^2 x$ to form quadratic $3\cot^2 x - \cot x - 2 = 0$.
Solves quadratic to get $\cot x = 1$ and $\cot x = -\frac{2}{3}$ (or $\tan x = 1, -1.5$).
Obtains $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$ (or $0.785$) and $x = 2.16$ rad and no others in $0 \le x \le \pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: using double angle substitution cos(2theta) = 1 - 2sin^2(theta) to solve equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Double angle cosine substitution creating quadratic in sine.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$ into the equation:
$$2(1 - 2\sin^2\theta) + 3\sin\theta = 2$$
$$2 - 4\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta = 2$$
$$4\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta = 0$$

Factorise the equation:
$$\sin\theta(4\sin\theta - 3) = 0 \implies \sin\theta = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad \sin\theta = \frac{3}{4}$$

Solve in the interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\sin\theta = 0 \implies \theta = 0^\circ, 180^\circ, 360^\circ$$
$$\sin\theta = 0.75 \implies \theta = \arcsin(0.75) \approx 48.6^\circ, \quad 180^\circ - 48.59^\circ = 131.4^\circ$$
$$\theta = 0^\circ, 48.6^\circ, 131.4^\circ, 180^\circ, 360^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies double angle identity $\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$ to form quadratic $4\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta = 0$.
Factorises $\sin\theta(4\sin\theta - 3) = 0$ to get $\sin\theta = 0$ and $\sin\theta = 0.75$.
Obtains $\theta = 0^\circ, 48.6^\circ, 131.4^\circ, 180^\circ, 360^\circ$ and no others in interval.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: transforming secant/tangent equation to quadratic form and finding radian solutions.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Show that secant/tangent equation reduces to quadratic in tangent.

hints: Recall the Pythagorean identity connecting secant and tangent: $\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x$.
Substitute $1 + \tan^2 x$ in place of $\sec^2 x$: $2(1 + \tan^2 x) + \tan x = 5$.
Expand the brackets and subtract $5$ from both sides to form $2\tan^2 x + \tan x - 3 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the identity $\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x$:
$$2(1 + \tan^2 x) + \tan x = 5$$

Expand and collect like terms on the left:
$$2 + 2\tan^2 x + \tan x = 5$$
$$2\tan^2 x + \tan x + 2 - 5 = 0$$
$$2\tan^2 x + \tan x - 3 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes identity $\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x$ into the given equation.
Expands $2(1 + \tan^2 x) + \tan x = 5$ and collects all terms on one side.
Obtains given 3-term quadratic $2\tan^2 x + \tan x - 3 = 0$ with no intermediate errors.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving quadratic in tangent over [0, pi].

hints: Factorise $2\tan^2 x + \tan x - 3 = 0$ as $(2\tan x + 3)(\tan x - 1) = 0$.
For $\tan x = 1$ in $0 \le x \le \pi$, the exact solution is $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$.
For $\tan x = -1.5$, tangent is negative in Quadrant II: $x = \pi - \arctan(1.5) \approx 3.1416 - 0.9828 = 2.16$ rad.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise the quadratic in $\tan x$:
$$(2\tan x + 3)(\tan x - 1) = 0 \implies \tan x = 1 \quad \text{or} \quad \tan x = -\frac{3}{2}$$

Solve $\tan x = 1$ for $0 \le x \le \pi$:
$$x = \arctan(1) = \frac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.785 \text{ rad}$$

Solve $\tan x = -1.5$ in Quadrant II for $0 \le x \le \pi$:
$$x = \pi - \arctan(1.5) = \pi - 0.98279... \approx 2.1588 \approx 2.16 \text{ rad}$$
$$x = \frac{\pi}{4}, \ 2.16 \text{ rad}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Factorises into $(2\tan x + 3)(\tan x - 1) = 0$ and finds at least one valid root for $\tan x$.
Obtains $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$ (or $0.785$) and $x = 2.16$ rad and no other solutions in $0 \le x \le \pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: cosecant/cotangent quadratic reduction with double angle domain solving in degrees.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proof that reciprocal cosecant/cotangent equation transforms into quadratic in cotangent.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $\operatorname{cosec}^2 2\theta = 1 + \cot^2 2\theta$:
$$4(1 + \cot^2 2\theta) - 7 = \cot 2\theta$$

Expand and collect all terms on one side:
$$4 + 4\cot^2 2\theta - 7 = \cot 2\theta$$
$$4\cot^2 2\theta - \cot 2\theta - 3 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes identity $\operatorname{cosec}^2 2\theta = 1 + \cot^2 2\theta$ into the equation.
Expands $4(1 + \cot^2 2\theta) - 7 = \cot 2\theta$ and collects terms.
Obtains $4\cot^2 2\theta - \cot 2\theta - 3 = 0$ with complete correct working.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving double-angle cotangent quadratic across full period in degrees.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise the quadratic in $\cot 2\theta$:
$$(4\cot 2\theta + 3)(\cot 2\theta - 1) = 0$$
$$\cot 2\theta = 1 \implies \tan 2\theta = 1$$
$$\cot 2\theta = -\frac{3}{4} \implies \tan 2\theta = -\frac{4}{3}$$

Find solutions for $2\theta \in [0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ from $\tan 2\theta = 1$:
$$2\theta = 45^\circ, 225^\circ \implies \theta = 22.5^\circ, 112.5^\circ$$

Find solutions for $2\theta \in [0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ from $\tan 2\theta = -\frac{4}{3}$:
$$\text{Reference angle} = \arctan(4/3) \approx 53.13^\circ$$
$$2\theta = 180^\circ - 53.13^\circ = 126.87^\circ \implies \theta \approx 63.4^\circ$$
$$2\theta = 360^\circ - 53.13^\circ = 306.87^\circ \implies \theta \approx 153.4^\circ$$
$$\theta = 22.5^\circ, 63.4^\circ, 112.5^\circ, 153.4^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Factorises into $(4\cot 2\theta + 3)(\cot 2\theta - 1) = 0$ to find $\cot 2\theta = 1, -0.75$ (or $\tan 2\theta = 1, -\frac{4}{3}$).
Finds angles for $2\theta$ in interval $0^\circ \le 2\theta \le 360^\circ$ (e.g. $45^\circ, 126.9^\circ, 225^\circ, 306.9^\circ$).
Obtains all four solutions $\theta = 22.5^\circ, 63.4^\circ, 112.5^\circ, 153.4^\circ$ and no others in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: double angle cosine reduction to quadratic and quadratic formula solution in degrees.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Double angle cosine substitution producing quadratic in cosine.

hints: Use the double angle identity $\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1$.
Expand to get $6\cos^2 x - 3 = 5\cos x - 1$, then add $1$ and subtract $5\cos x$ to reach $6\cos^2 x - 5\cos x - 2 = 0$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1$:
$$3(2\cos^2 x - 1) = 5\cos x - 1$$

Expand and collect all terms on the left side:
$$6\cos^2 x - 3 = 5\cos x - 1$$
$$6\cos^2 x - 5\cos x - 2 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes double angle identity $\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1$ into $3\cos 2x = 5\cos x - 1$.
Expands $3(2\cos^2 x - 1) = 5\cos x - 1$ and rearranges terms.
Obtains $6\cos^2 x - 5\cos x - 2 = 0$ with no algebraic errors.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving 3-term quadratic in cosine using quadratic formula.

hints: The positive root $\frac{5 + \sqrt{73}}{12} \approx 1.129 > 1$ has no real solutions.

Find the reference angle $\alpha = \arccos(0.29533) \approx 72.82^\circ$. The solutions in Quadrants II and III are $180^\circ - 72.82^\circ = 107.2^\circ$ and $180^\circ + 72.82^\circ = 252.8^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the quadratic formula to $6\cos^2 x - 5\cos x - 2 = 0$:
$$\cos x = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{25 - 4(6)(-2)}}{12} = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{73}}{12}$$

Evaluate both roots:
$$\cos x = \frac{5 + \sqrt{73}}{12} \approx 1.1287 \quad (\text{reject, since } \cos x \le 1)$$
$$\cos x = \frac{5 - \sqrt{73}}{12} \approx -0.29533$$

Find angles in $0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ$:
$$\text{Reference angle} = \arccos(0.29533) \approx 72.82^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant II: } x = 180^\circ - 72.82^\circ = 107.2^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant III: } x = 180^\circ + 72.82^\circ = 252.8^\circ$$
$$x = 107.2^\circ, 252.8^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies quadratic formula $\cos x = \frac{5 \pm \sqrt{73}}{12}$ and rejects root $> 1$.
Finds reference angle $\arccos(0.29533) \approx 72.82^\circ$ for $\cos x = \frac{5-\sqrt{73}}{12} \approx -0.2953$.
Obtains $x = 107.2^\circ$ and $x = 252.8^\circ$ and no other solutions in the interval.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: double angle tangent and cotangent elimination leading to a two-branch linear tangent solution.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Double angle tangent expansion combined with reciprocal cotangent.

hints: Multiply both sides by $\tan\theta(1 - \tan^2\theta)$ to get $6\tan^2\theta = 2(1 - \tan^2\theta)$, then collect terms to reach $4\tan^2\theta = 1$.

walkthrough.text:
Express both sides in terms of $\tan\theta$:
$$3\left(\frac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}\right) = 2\left(\frac{1}{\tan\theta}\right)$$
$$\frac{6\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta} = \frac{2}{\tan\theta}$$

Cross-multiply by $\tan\theta(1 - \tan^2\theta)$:
$$6\tan^2\theta = 2(1 - \tan^2\theta)$$
$$6\tan^2\theta = 2 - 2\tan^2\theta$$
$$8\tan^2\theta = 2 \implies 4\tan^2\theta = 1$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $\tan 2\theta = \frac{2\tan\theta}{1 - \tan^2\theta}$ and $\cot\theta = \frac{1}{\tan\theta}$.
Clears denominators to obtain $6\tan^2\theta = 2(1 - \tan^2\theta)$.
Rearranges to obtain $8\tan^2\theta = 2 \implies 4\tan^2\theta = 1$ correctly.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving square-root branches of tan^2(theta) in (0, 180).

walkthrough.text:
Take the square root of both sides:
$$\tan^2\theta = \frac{1}{4} \implies \tan\theta = \frac{1}{2} \quad \text{or} \quad \tan\theta = -\frac{1}{2}$$

Solve $\tan\theta = 0.5$ for $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
$$\theta = \arctan(0.5) \approx 26.565^\circ \approx 26.6^\circ$$

Solve $\tan\theta = -0.5$ for $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
$$\theta = 180^\circ - 26.565^\circ = 153.435^\circ \approx 153.4^\circ$$
$$\theta = 26.6^\circ, \ 153.4^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Solves for $\tan\theta = \pm\frac{1}{2} = \pm 0.5$.
Calculates reference angle $\arctan(0.5) \approx 26.57^\circ$ and identifies Quadrant II angle $180^\circ - 26.57^\circ$.
Obtains $\theta = 26.6^\circ$ and $\theta = 153.4^\circ$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Capstone: comprehensive proof of cot(x) - tan(x) = 2cot(2x) and exact equation solving in radians.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proof of fundamental double angle cotangent relationship from quotient definition.

hints: Write $\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}$ and $\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$.
Combine over a common denominator: $\frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\sin x\cos x}$.
Recall double angle identities: $\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = \cos 2x$ and $\sin x\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x$.

walkthrough.text:
Express LHS in terms of sine and cosine:
$$\cot x - \tan x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$$

Combine fractions over the common denominator $\sin x\cos x$:
$$\frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\sin x\cos x}$$

Substitute double angle identities $\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x$ and $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$:
$$\frac{\cos 2x}{\frac{1}{2}\sin 2x} = 2\left(\frac{\cos 2x}{\sin 2x}\right) = 2\cot 2x$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses LHS as $\frac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\sin x\cos x}$.
Applies double angle identity $\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x$ to the numerator.
Applies denominator identity $\sin x\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x$.
Concludes $\frac{\cos 2x}{\frac{1}{2}\sin 2x} = 2\frac{\cos 2x}{\sin 2x} = 2\cot 2x$ with complete logic.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exact solution in radians using established double angle cotangent identity.

hints: For $0 < x < \pi$, the domain for $2x$ is $0 < 2x < 2\pi$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute the identity from part (a):
$$2\cot 2x = 2\sqrt{3} \implies \cot 2x = \sqrt{3}$$
$$\tan 2x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

Find all angles for $2x$ in the interval $0 < 2x < 2\pi$:
$$2x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \quad 2x = \frac{\pi}{6} + \pi = \frac{7\pi}{6}$$

Divide by 2 to find exact values of $x$:
$$x = \frac{\pi}{12}, \quad x = \frac{7\pi}{12}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Replaces LHS to obtain $2\cot 2x = 2\sqrt{3} \implies \cot 2x = \sqrt{3} \implies \tan 2x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Finds valid roots for $2x \in (0, 2\pi)$: $2x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}$.
Obtains exact solutions $x = \frac{\pi}{12}$ and $x = \frac{7\pi}{12}$ and no others in $0 < x < \pi$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Capstone: proving cosecant-cotangent half-angle identity and solving resulting non-factorisable quadratic equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proof that cosecant minus cotangent of double angle equals tangent.

walkthrough.text:
Expand the numerator and denominator using double angle identities:
$$\frac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{\sin 2\theta} = \frac{1 - (1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{2\sin^2\theta}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}$$

Cancel $2\sin\theta$:
$$\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta$$

Split the left-hand fraction into reciprocal functions:
$$\frac{1}{\sin 2\theta} - \frac{\cos 2\theta}{\sin 2\theta} = \operatorname{cosec} 2\theta - \cot 2\theta$$
$$\operatorname{cosec} 2\theta - \cot 2\theta \equiv \tan\theta$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $\cos 2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$ into the numerator to get $1 - (1 - 2\sin^2\theta) = 2\sin^2\theta$.
Substitutes $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and cancels $2\sin\theta$ to reach $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta$.
Splits fraction $\frac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{\sin 2\theta} = \frac{1}{\sin 2\theta} - \frac{\cos 2\theta}{\sin 2\theta}$.
Concludes $\operatorname{cosec} 2\theta - \cot 2\theta \equiv \tan\theta$ clearly.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving equation using deduced half-angle identity and quadratic formula.

hints: Use quadratic formula: $\sin\theta = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4} \approx 0.7808$ (rejecting negative root $< -1$). Find angles in Quadrants I and II.

walkthrough.text:
Replace LHS with $\tan\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = 2\cos\theta \implies \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = 2\cos\theta \implies \sin\theta = 2\cos^2\theta$$

Use $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$ to form a quadratic in $\sin\theta$:
$$\sin\theta = 2(1 - \sin^2\theta) = 2 - 2\sin^2\theta$$
$$2\sin^2\theta + \sin\theta - 2 = 0$$

Apply the quadratic formula:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(2)(-2)}}{4} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}$$
$$\sin\theta = \frac{-1 + \sqrt{17}}{4} \approx 0.780776 \quad (\text{reject } \frac{-1-\sqrt{17}}{4} < -1)$$

Find solutions in $0^\circ < \theta < 360^\circ$:
$$\text{Reference angle} = \arcsin(0.780776) \approx 51.33^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant I: } \theta = 51.3^\circ$$
$$\text{Quadrant II: } \theta = 180^\circ - 51.33^\circ = 128.7^\circ$$
$$\theta = 51.3^\circ, \ 128.7^\circ$$

ai_rubric.observable: Replaces LHS with $\tan\theta$ to write $\tan\theta = 2\cos\theta \implies \sin\theta = 2\cos^2\theta$.
Substitutes $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$ to form $2\sin^2\theta + \sin\theta - 2 = 0$.
Solves quadratic formula to find valid root $\sin\theta = \frac{-1+\sqrt{17}}{4} \approx 0.7808$ (rejecting root $< -1$).
Obtains $\theta = 51.3^\circ$ and $\theta = 128.7^\circ$ and no other solutions in range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Capstone: compound angle linear reduction and exact angle solving in degrees.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Compound angle expansions on both sides simplified using exact surd values.

hints: Expand both sides using compound angle formulae: $\cos(x + 60^\circ) = \cos x\cos 60^\circ - \sin x\sin 60^\circ$ and $\sin(x - 30^\circ) = \sin x\cos 30^\circ - \cos x\sin 30^\circ$.
Multiply by 2 to clear fractions: $2\cos x - 2\sqrt{3}\sin x = 3\sqrt{3}\sin x - 3\cos x$.
Collect $\cos x$ on the left and $\sin x$ on the right: $5\cos x = 5\sqrt{3}\sin x \implies \tan x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand both sides with compound angle formulae:
$$2(\cos x\cos 60^\circ - \sin x\sin 60^\circ) = 3(\sin x\cos 30^\circ - \cos x\sin 30^\circ)$$

Substitute exact trigonometric values:
$$2\left(\frac{1}{2}\cos x - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x\right) = 3\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x - \frac{1}{2}\cos x\right)$$
$$\cos x - \sqrt{3}\sin x = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x - \frac{3}{2}\cos x$$

Multiply throughout by 2 and group like terms:
$$2\cos x - 2\sqrt{3}\sin x = 3\sqrt{3}\sin x - 3\cos x$$
$$5\cos x = 5\sqrt{3}\sin x$$
$$\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \frac{5}{5\sqrt{3}} \implies \tan x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$
